subtitle: On Kurma Pitha, a king carves his kingdom’s heart in stone and water

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of the temple hill at dusk
panels.action: Dhanya Manikya stands on a rise facing the tortoise-shaped hill, the outline of the Tripura Sundari temple rising above Kalyan Sagar’s still waters under a deepening sky.

dialogue.text: On a tortoise hill beside a still tank, Dhanya Manikya raised Matabari—where royal power, Shakta devotion and Bengali craft fused into the living heart of Tripura.

i18n.hi: कछुए जैसी पहाड़ी और शांत ताल के पास धन्य माणिक्य ने माताबाड़ी उठाई—जहाँ राजसत्ता, शक्तिभक्ति और बंगाली शिल्प मिलकर त्रिपुरा की धड़कन बने।

panels.shot: slow push-in from aerial view of Udaipur valley and Kurma-shaped hill
panels.action: From high above, the landscape of Udaipur spreads out—forests, scattered settlements and a distinct hill shaped like a tortoise, with Dhanya Manikya and his retinue tiny at its base.

dialogue.text: Around 1501, in the forests of Tripura, a new capital was taking shape at Udaipur, and a tortoise-shaped hill waited, bare and silent.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1501 में, त्रिपुरा के जंगलों में उदयपुर नाम की नई राजधानी बन रही थी, और कछुए-सी पहाड़ी नंगी, शांत पड़ी थी।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Dhanya Manikya in council tent
panels.action: Inside a royal pavilion, Dhanya Manikya sits upright on a low throne, scrolls and palm-leaf manuscripts before him, as courtiers and priests stand respectfully in the lamplight.

dialogue.text: Dhanya Manikya, king of Tripura, strengthened his hill kingdom between Bengal’s plains and the hills of the northeast, seeking a center that could bind warriors, farmers and priests.

i18n.hi: त्रिपुरा के राजा धन्य माणिक्य ने बंगाल की मैदानी धरती और उत्तर-पूर्व की पहाड़ियों के बीच अपने पहाड़ी राज्य को मजबूत किया, एक ऐसा केंद्र खोजते हुए जो सैनिकों, किसानों और पुजारियों को जोड़े।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot, low light, Dhanya half-lit by oil lamp
panels.action: At night, Dhanya Manikya sits alone, a single oil lamp casting shadows as he studies a small metal image of a goddess, his face thoughtful and intent.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala later spoke of dreams and visions of Tripura Sundari, but the records we can touch show a king who chose Shakta devotion as his kingdom’s public soul.

i18n.hi: राजमाला बाद में सपनों और त्रिपुरा सुंदरी के दर्शन की बातें करती है, पर हमारे पास जो रिकॉर्ड हैं, वे एक ऐसे राजा को दिखाते हैं जिसने शक्तिभक्ति को अपने राज्य की सार्वजनिक आत्मा बनाया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dhanya speaking with a senior Brahmin architect beside a rough hill sketch
panels.action: Dhanya Manikya gestures toward a rough drawing of the tortoise-shaped hill on a palm leaf, while an elderly Brahmin architect holds a measuring cord and listens intently.

dialogue.speaker: dhanya_manikya
dialogue.text: On Kurma Pitha, the Mother must sit—stone above, sacred water below.

i18n.hi: कूर्म पिठ पर माँ को बैठना ही होगा—ऊपर पत्थर, नीचे पवित्र जल।

panels.shot: wide shot of hill base with surveyors and workers
panels.action: At the foot of the hill, Dhanya Manikya watches as surveyors stretch ropes, mark lines with chalk, and artisans examine soil and stone, the forest partially cleared around them.

dialogue.text: Tradition calls the hill Kurma Pitha, the tortoise seat. Whether or not Sati’s body ever fell here, Dhanya chose it deliberately, giving legend a visible, royal form.

i18n.hi: परंपरा इस पहाड़ी को कूर्म पिठ, कछुए की आसन, कहती है। सती का शरीर सच में यहाँ गिरा या नहीं, धन्य ने इसे सोच-समझकर चुना, दंतकथा को राजसी रूप देकर।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on Dhanya greeting craftsmen from Bengal
panels.action: A group of Bengali temple craftsmen, in simple dhotis and carrying tools, bow to Dhanya Manikya as he steps forward to receive them with measured dignity.

dialogue.text: He summoned artisans who knew the new roof forms of Bengal. The temple would be Ek-ratna—one tower, rising like a grain store above curved roofs, in the style spreading from the Ganga plains.

i18n.hi: उसने उन कारीगरों को बुलाया जो बंगाल की नई छतों के रूप जानते थे। मंदिर बनेगा एक-रत्न—एक मीनार, घुमावदार छतों के ऊपर ऐसे उठती जैसे अनाज का भंडार, गंगातट की चलन में।

panels.shot: architectural cutaway-style wide shot of temple skeleton rising
panels.action: The stone and brick skeleton of the temple rises on the hill—square sanctum walls, corner projections and a central plinth—while workers lift bricks in baskets and masons smooth wet mortar.

dialogue.text: Column by column, brick by brick, the Ek-ratna form grew: a square sanctum, rounded Bengal cornices, and a single shikhara that would mark Tripura’s skyline.

i18n.hi: स्तंभ पर स्तंभ, ईंट पर ईंट चढ़ती गई एक-रत्न की शक्ल: चौकोर गर्भगृह, गोलाई लिए बंगाली कार्निस, और एक ही शिखर जो त्रिपुरा की रेखा तय करेगा।

panels.shot: medium close-up of artisans shaping the curved cornice roofs
panels.action: Artisans on bamboo scaffolds carefully place bricks to form the gentle curve of the cornice, their hands steady, while Dhanya Manikya watches from below, eyes narrowed in concentration.

dialogue.text: The curved roof recalled huts of the delta and earlier thatch. In Matabari’s stone, local memory and new fashion met, giving Tripura a temple that felt both familiar and royal.

i18n.hi: मुड़ी हुई छत डेल्टा की झोपड़ियों और पुराने घासफूस की याद दिलाती थी। माताबाड़ी की पत्थर-देह में पुरानी याद और नई फैशन मिले, और त्रिपुरा को ऐसा मंदिर मिला जो अपना भी लगे, राजसी भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of laborers digging the tank beside the hill
panels.action: Scores of laborers dig a vast rectangular depression beside the hill, carrying soil away in baskets, as Dhanya Manikya stands under a shade canopy, surveying the future Kalyan Sagar.

dialogue.text: Beside the hill he ordered a tank cut into the earth—Kalyan Sagar. It would store water, reflect the shrine, and anchor the temple in both ritual and everyday life.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ी के बगल में उसने जमीन काटकर ताल बनवाया—कल्याण सागर। यह जल सहेजेगा, मंदिर का प्रतिबिंब दिखाएगा, और मंदिर को पूजा और रोज़मर्रा, दोनों में जड़ देगा।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from waterline of early Kalyan Sagar filling
panels.action: Water from a channel rushes into the freshly cut tank, ripples spreading across the surface as Dhanya Manikya steps down the unfinished ghat, resting his hand briefly on a stone step.

dialogue.text: In time, fish and turtles would glide in its depths, and the tank would be as sacred as the sanctum—not legend, but living ecosystem, tied to ritual and daily use.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ उसकी गहराइयों में मछलियाँ और कछुए तैरेंगे, और ताल भी गर्भगृह जितना पवित्र होगा—कथा नहीं, जीता-जागता पारिस्थितिक तंत्र, जो पूजा और रोजमर्रा से जुड़ा है।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on first turtles entering the tank, Dhanya in background
panels.action: A pair of black softshell turtles slip into the tank’s calm water near the ghat stairs, while Dhanya Manikya watches from above with quiet satisfaction.

dialogue.text: Later generations would protect the black softshell turtles of Kalyan Sagar as sacred, even as modern conservationists debate how ritual and endangered life can share the same water.

i18n.hi: आने वाली पीढ़ियाँ कल्याण सागर के काले सॉफ्टशेल कछुओं को पवित्र मानकर बचाएंगी, जबकि आधुनिक संरक्षक सोचेंगे कि पूजा और दुर्लभ जीव एक ही जल किस तरह बाँटें।

panels.shot: dim interior close-up of sanctum threshold
panels.action: The dark sanctum doorway frames Dhanya Manikya, bare-chested and reverent, pausing at the threshold as priests stand ready with incense and lamps behind him.

dialogue.text: Within the new walls, the sanctum awaited its image. Rajmala remembers a battle-companion idol, Chhoto-Ma, brought here by the king, turning a portable guardian into a fixed, public goddess.

i18n.hi: नई दीवारों के भीतर, गर्भगृह अपने विग्रह का इंतज़ार कर रहा था। राजमाला एक युद्ध-साथी देवी, ‘छोटो–मा’, को याद करती है, जिसे राजा यहाँ लाया, चलती-फिरती रक्षक को स्थिर, सार्वजनिक देवी बना दिया।

panels.shot: tight interior shot of small idol being placed on the pedestal
panels.action: Hands gently place a small dark stone image of the goddess on a low pedestal inside the sanctum, as Dhanya Manikya bows deeply, his crown removed and set aside.

dialogue.speaker: dhanya_manikya
dialogue.text: From the field to the hill, Mother, dwell now with my people.

i18n.hi: मैदान से पहाड़ी पर चलो, माँ—अब मेरे लोगों के बीच बसो।

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle interior of sanctum with ritual in progress
panels.action: Priests circle the goddess with lamps in an early consecration rite, flames tracing arcs in the dim space, while Dhanya Manikya offers a tray of flowers, his face lit by the glow.

dialogue.text: To some, Tripura Sundari was a fierce Tantric power; to others, a kindly Matabari—Mother of the hill. Dhanya’s temple let both understandings stand under one roof, one ritual sequence.

i18n.hi: किसी के लिए त्रिपुरा सुंदरी प्रचंड तांत्रिक शक्ति थी, किसी के लिए स्नेहिल माताबाड़ी—पहाड़ी की माँ। धन्य के मंदिर ने दोनों रूपों को एक ही छत, एक ही पूजा-क्रम में जगह दी।

panels.shot: exterior wide shot of completed temple with crowd at inaugural festival
panels.action: The completed Ek-ratna temple crowns the hill, its single tower rising above curved roofs, as a festival crowd gathers around the base and at the ghats, Dhanya Manikya seated beneath a canopy.

dialogue.text: When the temple opened, Tripura’s people climbed Kurma Pitha to see their king and goddess together. Architecture turned royal will and belief into a shared, repeated act.

i18n.hi: जब मंदिर खुला, त्रिपुरा के लोग कूर्म पिठ पर चढ़े—राजा और देवी को साथ देखने। शिल्प ने राज-इच्छा और आस्था को साझा, बार-बार दोहराए जाने वाला काम बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dhanya at the ghat, watching reflections
panels.action: Standing alone at the edge of Kalyan Sagar, Dhanya Manikya looks at the reflection of the temple shimmering on the water, his face calm yet burdened, hands clasped.

dialogue.text: No inscription from his hand survives to confirm the exact year, yet the style, the plan and later chronicles all point back to Dhanya’s reign and his deliberate shaping of Matabari.

i18n.hi: उसके अपने हाथ की कोई शिलालेख साल साफ़ नहीं बताती, पर शैली, योजना और बाद की कथाएँ सब धन्य के राज और उसकी सोची-समझी माताबाड़ी की रूप-रेखा की ओर इशारा करती हैं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing temple across centuries hinted by changing pilgrims
panels.action: The temple remains constant atop the hill while the pilgrims at its base subtly change in dress and number across three blended bands, hinting at centuries passing under the same tower.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the same Ek-ratna silhouette still crowns Udaipur. Rituals, politics and practice have shifted, yet the hill, the tank and the shrine continue to frame Tripura’s public life.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी वही एक-रत्न आकृति उदयपुर के सिर पर है। पूजा, सत्ता और व्यवहार बदल गए, पर पहाड़ी, ताल और मंदिर आज भी त्रिपुरा के सार्वजनिक जीवन की चौखट बने हैं।

panels.shot: contemplative aerial pull-back from temple and tank at sunrise
panels.action: At sunrise, the temple and Kalyan Sagar glow in soft light, Dhanya Manikya’s figure imagined as a faint ghostly silhouette on the hill, fading as the camera pulls high above the landscape.

dialogue.text: On Kurma Pitha, Dhanya Manikya showed how stone and water can turn devotion into an institution—binding memory, environment and authority long after the king himself has vanished.

i18n.hi: कूर्म पिठ पर धन्य माणिक्य ने दिखाया कि पत्थर और पानी भक्ति को संस्था में बदल सकते हैं—याद, पर्यावरण और सत्ता को बाँधते हुए, बहुत बाद तक, जब राजा स्वयं मिट चुका हो।

subtitle_i18n.en: On Kurma Pitha, a king carves his kingdom’s heart in stone and water
subtitle_i18n.hi: कूर्म पिठ पर, राजा ने पत्थर और पानी में अपने राज्य का दिल गढ़ा
